title: Bakit, Papa?
author: Melissa O. Yuson
excerpt: Sa usapang pamilyang Pilipino, may iba’t ibang eksena ang haligi nito
body:
Sa usapang pamilyang Pilipino, may iba’t ibang eksena ang haligi nito:

(Supportive)
Dito, ang aking entablado ay ang pintuan
nakapamewang habang katabi si bantay,
nag-aantay
kay itay

Bakit, Papa? Bakit kahit na ikaw ay pagod,
kahit ikaw ang nagpako ng bubong
para may pamamahayang silong,
nagawa mo pa rin akong
bigyan ng pasalubong?

(Yearning)
Dito, ang aking entablado ay siya pa ring pintuan
katatapos maghugas ng pinggan,
kamay ay pinunasan,
cellphone ay dali-daling binuksan

Bakit, Papa? Bakit kita ko pa rin ang saya
‘pagkat kahit ang signal ay mahina,
parang katabi lang kita,
mag-ingat ka, Pa,
riyan sa ibang bansa.

(Angry)
Hindi pa rin ako napapagal dito sa pinto
ang buwan ang karamay
hindi rin mangangalay,
para kay tatay

Bakit, Papa? Masalimuot ipaglaban ang bayan
ngunit galit man ako dahil nangungulila,
dahil imbis na nasa bahay ka,
ay ikaw ay nasa kalsada
lubos pa rin kitang naiintindihan, Papa.

(Flirty)
Ang entablado ay hindi akin
ako lamang ay ekstra rito,
hinding hindi aayaw,
kung pangalan niya ang ihihiyaw

“Bakit, Papa?”— Ang tanong na ito ay hindi akin,
ito’y galing sa kanilang hindi nakaiintindi
kung bakit daw may Papa na malambot,
may Papa na kumekembot,
may Papa na maharot

Papa ko siya,
nandiyan at matiyaga,
sa paraang malaya,
maging tulad niyang Papa rin ang gusto niya.

Ngayong araw ng mga haligi ng tahanan, ipinagdiriwang ang mga kuwentong nagpapatibay dito. Sa mga amang pagod pero may dala pa ring pasalubong, sa mga tatay na puspos ang kayod sa ibang bansa, sa mga nasa kalsada’t nakikibaka, gayundin sa mga papa na mama mama ang atake, at sa lahat ng mga nagsilbing ama at umakay sa agos ng buhay— maligayang 𝗔𝗿𝗮𝘄 𝗻𝗴 𝗺𝗴𝗮 𝗔𝗺𝗮!

title: TSU, inaasahang magpatupad ng online classes; TSUians, nananawagan para sa total suspension
author: Renz Joshua D.T. De Vera
excerpt: Kasunod ng walang-tigil na pag-ulan, pagguho ng mga tulay, at pagdedeklara ng state of calamity sa ilang bahagi ng Tarlac, ibinahagi ni Tarlac State University Supreme Student Council (TSU-SSC) President Jazzmine Samson ang shift sa…
body:
Kasunod ng walang-tigil na pag-ulan, pagguho ng mga tulay, at pagdedeklara ng state of calamity sa ilang bahagi ng Tarlac, ibinahagi ni Tarlac State University Supreme Student Council (TSU-SSC) President Jazzmine Samson ang shift sa online classes at work-from-home set-up ng pamantasan sa paparating na linggo, mula August 31 hanggang September 5. 

Bagaman hinihintay pa ang opisyal na pahayag ng unibersidad, marami na sa mga estudyante ang patuloy na nananawagan para sa total class suspension kaysa sa proposed na shift sa online learning modality. 

“I understand that the current decisions of TSU and SSC are tentative/reactive to the situation as of now, but shifting to alternative learning methods such as online classes only solved part of the problem,” pahayag ni Darrel Joshua sa isang post sa Firefox League, isang Facebook group ng TSUian community. 

Dagdag pa rito, pangamba rin ng mga estudyante na magiging dagdag-alalahanin ang mga online activities ngayong paparating na linggo, na sasabay sa perwisyong dulot ng walang tigil na pag-ulan at patuloy na pagtaas ng baha sa kanilang mga komunidad.
“Bilang isang estudyante, labis po akong nag-aalala dahil marami po sa amin ang kasalukuyang nasa mahirap na kalagayan. 

Naiintindihan po namin na wala pa namang opisyal na activity o requirements na ipinapagawa sa amin, ngunit hindi po namin maiiwasang isipin at alalahanin kung paano namin haharapin ang mga ito kung sakaling magsimula na ang online classes,” paliwanag ni Crisel Lansang. 

Matatandaang kinansela ng TSU ang dapat sanang Flexible Learning Week ngayong paparating na linggo bunsod ng ‘di inaasahang class suspensions sa unang bahagi ng Agosto dahil sa sunod-sunod na pag-ulang dulot ng Habagat. 

Sa mga sandaling ito, wala pang opisyal na kumpirmasyon ang unibersidad hinggil sa magiging guidelines at working schedules ngayong nasa gitna ng sakuna ang lalawigan, habang ibinahagi naman ni Samson na patuloy ang pakikipag-ugnayan ng konseho sa administrasyon ng TSU para sa total suspension ng mga klase.

Inaabisuhan naman ang mga mag-aaral na maghintay sa pormal na anunsyo nito sa mga susunod na oras.

title: TSU to allow gender-affirmative dress code in 2026 grad rites
author: Andrei P. Opeña
excerpt: After long years of strict adherence to gender-specific graduation attire, Tarlac State University (TSU) will now allow its 2026 batch of graduating students, especially transgender and gender non-conforming (TGNC) students, to wear…
body:
After long years of strict adherence to gender-specific graduation attire, Tarlac State University (TSU) will now allow its 2026 batch of graduating students, especially transgender and gender non-conforming (TGNC) students, to wear attire aligned with their gender identity during their graduation rites this coming July.

This comes following the approval of the proposed amendments to the Graduation Attire Guidelines for Batch 2026 after years of continuous dialogue and consultation, as announced by the TSU Office of the Student Regent (OSR) on May 16.

While the amendments may still need further improvements, the office, in a statement posted on Facebook, said that “this development marks a significant and meaningful step toward strengthening gender responsiveness, inclusivity, and student representation within the Tarlac State University community.”

It added that while progress all at once may not be easy to achieve, “every policy improved, every space opened, and every voice recognized reflects a community that continues to move forward.”

The office recognized the Safe Space Society (TSU-SSS), which has been moving to promote inclusivity and the welfare of the entire TSUian student community.

It likewise acknowledged the Offices of Gender and Development, Admission and Registration, Student Affairs and Services, Vice President for Academic Affairs, and the University President for their support and approval of the student-led initiative.

Below are the amended and approved graduation attire guidelines for the graduating class of 2026:
• For Cisgender Men and Trans Men: Cream/beige barong (non-see-through), black seda pants, and black formal shoes.
• For Cisgender Women: Cream/beige Filipiniana top or dress, long skirt (must not be above knee length), and cream/beige heels (closed-toe maximum of 2 inches).
• For Trans Women: Cream/beige Filipiniana top (dress not permitted), cream/beige flare pants, or any type of long pants (skirts not permitted), and cream/beige heels (closed-toe maximum of 2 inches).

The office, however, despite the new guidelines, noted that all graduation attire must uphold the formality of the ceremony, thus, prohibiting above-the-knee high slits and low-back and low front-cut Filipinianas. 

Meanwhile, in a comment, former President of the TSU-SSS Mx. Nixe David Alviar expressed their elation with the approval, saying “Sa wakas! Matapos ang ilang taon sa pakikibaka ng isang tunay na ligtas na espasyo, sa isang tunay na “Unity in Inclusivity”, may usad na.”

It could be noted that in 2025, student councils, publications, and various student organizations issued a joint statement calling for the immediate approval, institutionalization, and full implementation of the Gender-Responsive Policy.

Now, such an effort, alongside the collective action and continued collaboration between the Supreme Student Council (SSC) and the TSU-SSS, has resulted in meaningful progress in the students’ fight for inclusivity. 

On the other hand, the TSU-SSS, in a separate statement, proudly celebrated the approval, deeming it as not merely a policy change but a “recognition of every student’s right to dignity, authenticity, and representation."

“Through collective action, dialogue, and student-led advocacy, we have shown that meaningful change is possible when institutions choose inclusivity and empathy,” it added.

Amidst this, both the OSR and TSU-SSS vowed to remain committed to championing policies and spaces aimed at upholding the rights, dignity, and recognition of students’ identity moving forward as there is “still more work to be done.”

title: Out of Touch
author: Janeth G. Gamboa
excerpt: People say ‘living under a rock’ means being clueless about the world. But the real problem does not lie in ignorance—it is stubbornness. Some folks know what is happening but refuse to let reality seep in.
body:
People say ‘living under a rock’ means being clueless about the world. But the real problem does not lie in ignorance—it is stubbornness. Some folks know what is happening but refuse to let reality seep in. Their minds are rock-hard, sealed against the clamor of their constituents’ testimonies. It is not about being out of touch—but choosing to stay out of touch despite the opportunities to be rightfully swayed and perceive truth.

It is much of a dismay for the department that is supposed to oversee the nation’s spending and economic well-being to fail. In mathematics, calculations are done to seek the answer. But one cannot calculate without understanding the problem in the first place. In its stead, it will birth a wrong answer that does not correspond to reality.

True to its horror, the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) insists that a mere P500 is enough for a Noche Buena meal for many Filipino families. The DTI Secretary, Cristina A. Roque, stated that it is adequate for a family of four, citing the DTI Price Guide for the usual dishes served in Noche Buena: Christmas ham can be had at P170, spaghetti for P78.50, with spaghetti noodles at P30, and the sauce at P48.50. Then, macaroni salad would cost a total of P152.44, noodles at P40.95, mayonnaise at P55, and cheese at P56.60. Fruit salad at P98.25, as the fruit cocktail is priced at P61.75, and all-purpose cream at P36.25.

Well, it is enough—that is if we close our eyes and pretend we live in the 90s. In a blink, it is evident that it is not enough with the price tags stamped on groceries nowadays. It does not by a single spectacle represent the real cost of preparing a Christmas meal. The DTI’s numbers were plucked from the shelf holding the smallest-sized, cheapest brand, and there was utter disregard for the reality and struggles most families face when checking out.

The tragedy is not just in the numbers but the lived experiences of ordinary Filipinos, with low wages paired with such high living costs that burden many households and their purchasing power. The minimum wage in Metro Manila is P695 per day, with other regions’ remaining as low as P400. For some, P500 is already spent as fare or for gas to get home to their loved ones for the holidays.

In reality, the cost of a basic Noche Buena cart ranges from P1,000 to even P5,000. Evidently, let’s be clear: price inflation in the Philippines is at crisis level. The Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) has shown that the cost of basic food needs has far exceeded the wages of most families. According to the 2024 Occupational Wages Survey, the national average monthly wage of full-time workers was PHP 21,544. Meanwhile, basic survival in Manila, according to the private sector, requires PHP 20,000 to PHP 25,000 per month. Worse, that’s just for basic nutrition, not the special dishes and elements that make Christmas, Christmas.

Just how high up are the chairs they sit on that they fail to even look over towards the bottom? Noche Buena is not just any meal—it is about tradition, bonding, and celebrating one of the most awaited holidays, Christmas. In hope that even for one night, every Filipino family can gather together and enjoy delicious food filled with love. It is nothing but an insult for many families, as if the very message tells of a poor edition of a Christmas meal.

When corrupt officials steal millions from the masses, feast on the money, and spend thousands on platters and platters of gluttonous greed, it is hypocritical to coax the public to not spend so much. Just like what Kilusang Magbubukid ng Pilipinas (KMP) suggests to officials, why don’t they try to serve a P500 Noche Buena for their families to see if they can make their own numbers work? In truth, they do not even have the word “budget” on their tongues, when they can mindlessly spend thousands on steak, wine, fireworks, and gifts without batting an eye.

In the end, the DTI’s P500 Noche Buena claim is not just an accounting error—it is a failure. What they can do is not romanticize a low-cost meal and think we are contented by that, but rather make sure that Christmas products, not only in the range of Noche Buena, are affordable for Filipinos. It is high time to step down from the blinding glory of their thrones and to open their eyes to the struggles of everyday Filipinos. Anything less is not just out of touch—it is unforgivable. Especially during the season of joy, Christmas.

title: TSU yields 50 new psychometricians in 2026 PmLE, first-time takers surpass nat'l passing rate
author: Trixie L. Galulu
body:
A total of 50 Bachelor of Arts in Psychology graduates of Tarlac State University (TSU) passed the September 2026 Psychometricians Licensure Examination (PmLE), per the results released by the Professional Regulation Commission (PRC), September 23.

The university produced an 89.29% institutional passing rate, following closely behind the 91.73% passing rate posted by all examinees from all universities and colleges in the Philippines.

Meanwhile, TSU’s performance stood out further among its first-time takers, who recorded a 94.12% passing rate, outperforming both its overall standing and the national average.

The Work congratulates all the newly licensed TSUian psychometricians, wishing you all success in your future endeavors.

title: Recalling the Horrors
excerpt: The country is living in the past. More than five decades have passed since the late president, Ferdinand Marcos Sr.
body:
The country is living in the past. More than five decades have passed since the late president, Ferdinand Marcos Sr. had placed the whole nation under Martial Law, which legalized the arrest of opposition figures, journalists, and activists on the night after the signing of Proclamation No. 1081. 

The Work, the official student publication of Tarlac State University recognizes the 54th anniversary of the declaration of Martial Law in the Philippines. The Work vehemently recalls the dreadful era of suspending the constitution, dissolving the legislature, and ruling by decree. 

Numerous historical documents have demonstrated that during the Martial Law era, there were numerous human rights abuses in the areas of arrest and detention, enforced disappearances, murders, and torture of those who opposed his decree. An estimated 3,240 people died, 34,000 were tortured, and 70,000 were imprisoned. Numerous Filipinos who witnessed and experienced the numerous atrocities committed during that period have acknowledged that the Marcos era caused them to suffer psychologically and physically, and that daily survival has been a fascinating concept in their lives.

In line with this, The Work stands in solidarity with the victims of the past dictatorship, while fervently highlighting that the Martial Law era is nothing but a blatant personal greed of the Marcoses that had left the Philippines to downfall due to the horrors of social injustices, extreme corruption, and abuse of power. 

History may repeat itself, for the incumbent president looks and acts exactly like his father. What was once practiced by his parents has become the legacy of their family—and that is to control, dictate, and extract the country off of its resources, leaving it economically paralyzed for years. 

But we will not be silenced. Allowing a dictator’s son to lead is nothing but a mistake that the nation must never commit again. 
It is imperative that we never allow the bloody past to recur and condemn this country to any more atrocities or potential dictatorship. The Work honors the struggles and hardships of the Filipino masses, who have been the most vulnerable victims of the iron-fisted tyrant, alongside the silenced journalists and activists.

In addition to commemorating the 54th anniversary of the blood of those courageous enough to stand up and defend the voiceless and oppressed, may this day serve as a reminder that we are still fighting to preserve democracy, which was once taken from us.
Let us not forget. Never again.

title: COMSELEC commissioner calls for “peaceful election” amid council controversies
author: Kleyn Abigail F. Fernandez
excerpt: With the recent split and ongoing dispute within the incumbent Supreme Student Council (SSC), Committee on Student Elections (COMSELEC) commissioner and Screening Officer Lance Navarro criticized the involved parties for allegedly being…
body:
With the recent split and ongoing dispute within the incumbent Supreme Student Council (SSC), Committee on Student Elections (COMSELEC) commissioner and Screening Officer Lance Navarro criticized the involved parties for allegedly being “too invested in ruining each other’s images” instead of addressing pressing concerns within the University amid the campaign period.

“TSUians don’t deserve to see the things that you guys are doing. Hindi sagot ang bangayan ninyo sa dami ng problemang kailangang ayusin sa loob ng unibersidad,” he wrote in a statement posted on his Facebook account, May 16. 

“Some of you are speaking about “great leadership,” but at the same time, some of you cannot practice what you preach,” he added, encouraging the parties involved to address their concerns on the right platform.

Navarro’s statement also sparked discussions among students regarding due process, election integrity, and professionalism among student leaders during the campaign season.

𝗖𝗢𝗠𝗦𝗘𝗟𝗘𝗖 𝘂𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗿 𝗽𝘂𝗯𝗹𝗶𝗰 𝘀𝗰𝗿𝘂𝘁𝗶𝗻𝘆

Following the Facebook post, Navarro was questioned regarding the committee’s handling of separate issues involving “due process” in the disqualification case of a candidate, particularly on the alleged formality of the complaint and the recurring issue of grade qualifications which occurred last year.

“To add na rin, hindi na dapat umaabot pa sa VPAA ang isang disqualification case, lalo na’t kayo naman ang may hawak ng election at hindi ang OVPAA. Hindi ba kayang magdesisyon ng committee sa ganitong klaseng concern?” SSC President Brixter Millo asked.

Meanwhile, Navarro admitted the committee’s lapses regarding the failure to provide prior notice before the disqualification but remained firm on its basis, citing a “legal basis” anchored on the Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) signed by the candidates.

“Oo, may lapses ang committee. Hindi ka nabigyan ng notice bago i-disqualify. Pero huwag nating ihiwalay ang usapin sa mismong dahilan kung bakit ka nasampahan ng kaso in the first place,” Navarro replied.

“Hindi naman gawa-gawa lang ang issue. May legal basis iyon, at alam mo rin kung ano ang nakasaad sa Memorandum of Agreement na pinirmahan ninyo, kahit pa tinawag mo itong ‘ambiguous’ noong convenient na sa depensa mo,” he added.

The exchange of statements, which occurred a month ago, further escalated the unresolved conflicts within the student council, alongside allegations of troll farms and the circulation of defamatory statements on Facebook allegedly intended to damage the reputation of candidates vying for student council positions for the upcoming academic year.

𝗦𝗮𝗻𝗱𝗶𝗴𝗮𝗻 𝗖𝗼𝗹𝗹𝗶𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻

On April 11, SSC President Hon. Brixter Millo released a statement criticizing Vice President Rafael Jay Valix over what he described as “selective accountability” concerning issues involving alleged bullying, invasion of privacy, financial discrepancies, forgery, unresponsiveness within the council, and the growing division inside the SSC.

Following the public statement, Valix responded through a separate post, refuting the allegations and explaining that the questioned actions were carried out collectively due to the absence of the SSC president in order to avoid delays in processing university requirements.

The statement further revealed that the division within the SSC allegedly began following Intramurals 2026 and formally surfaced on February 25, 2026, separating the council into the so-called “Team President” and the “Core Committee.”

Meanwhile, in a recent published post of the Senator in Ways and Means, Euelle Dave Capulong, May 14, he expressed the ongoing dispute within the council, airing serious allegations of document forgery or bypassing of procedures, use of troll accounts, disrespectful behavior toward members of the university community, and alleged misuse of council funds. 

He also reaffirmed that the ongoing conflict within the council should not simply be labeled as a “personal conflict” as it affects the whole student body, and is a matter of public discourse and transparency.

“Nakakalungkot rin na sasabihin nilang personal na alitan iyan. In fact, hindi personal na alitan yan kung damay ang TSUians sa mga issues at kapabayaan nila,” he replied in a comment. 

𝗡𝗲𝘄 𝘀𝗹𝗮𝘁𝗲𝘀

Consequently, the unresolved conflict within the student council led to the formation of rival political factions, with Vice President Rafael Jay Valix and Senator on Audit Jazzmine Faye Samson leading Sandigan–TSU and Alon–TSU, respectively. 

Meanwhile, Patrick Kyle “Patricia Kyla” Frias of the TSU Safe Space Society (SSS) is also set to contest the presidential position under a newly formed political bloc, Ligtas–TSU.

As of writing, no official resolution has been publicly released regarding the issues raised between the opposing SSC factions and the questioned disqualification case ahead of the upcoming student elections later this May.

title: Bomb threat halts operations at TSU; campuses on lockdown as inspection underway
author: Clarisse T. Fajardo
excerpt: Midyear classes, enrollment, and other student activities in Tarlac State University (TSU) today have been suspended following an undisclosed report of a bomb threat received this morning, June 23.
body:
Midyear classes, enrollment, and other student activities in Tarlac State University (TSU) today have been suspended following an undisclosed report of a bomb threat received this morning, June 23. 

According to students at the Main Campus, security guards disallowed them from entering the school premises without a reason, finding out later that it was due to a reported bomb threat. 

“Actually, pagkadating namin sa campus, wala naman kaming kaalam-alam na may problem, (bomb threat) daw pala but understandable since biglaan. Pero that time pinapaalis kami sa campus,” an incoming second-year Psychology student shared.

“Na-frustrate and nagalit ako ng kaonti syempre. Pinapaalis na kami sa loob ng campus nang hindi malinaw na na-e-explain ‘yung sitwasyon. Hindi namin alam ang nangyayari at worried kami na baka maapektuhan ‘yung enrollment namin,” they added. 

Meanwhile, students were in TSU-Lucinda Campus due to classes and enrollment when they received the news.

Some initially took the situation lightly, but realized its severity when a security personnel intervened.

“Nung una akala po namin na joke joke lang siya hanggang sa may dumating po na guard and inabisuhan po kami na umuwi na po para raw po sa safety namin,” a College of Public Administration and Governance (CPAG) freshman said. 

“First time ko po na maka experience ng ganito, lalong lalo na po na kahapon din po ay may bomb threat po, nakakabahala po siya actually,” they added. 

Meanwhile, the security personnel of TSU said that upon receiving the information regarding the bomb threat, they immediately roamed around the campus and instructed students to go home. 

“Nung naka receive kami ng info sa taas na may bomb threat, bali inikot namin yung buong campus at nag room to room kami then pinauwi namin lahat, para na rin kasi sa safety ng mga bata,” the officer said in an interview. 

In light of this, all campuses of TSU were put on immediate lockdown as the Tarlac Police Provincial Office has yet to officially disclose results of the investigation.

TSU becomes one of the educational institutions in Tarlac to be targeted by a bomb threat this week, following similar incidents yesterday at the College of the Holy Spirit of Tarlac (CHST) and a private school in Barangay San Rafael. 

ADDENUM: In a statement released by the Tarlac City Government, after a thorough investigation, the PNP has confirmed that the bomb threat reports received by different schools and colleges were hoaxes. The link to the statement can be found here: https://www.facebook.com/share/p/1YkMpMVxRm/

title: TSU Intrams ‘26 budget, pitong buwan nang hindi mailabas
author: John Hermie M. Sarceda
body:
Pitong buwan matapos ang 2026 Tarlac State University (TSU) Intramurals, hindi pa rin nailalabas o naiproproseso ang ₱1.5 milyon na inilaan para sa gastusin ng mga atleta mula sa sampung kolehiyo ng pamantasan sa ilalim ng Supreme Student Council (SSC), dahilan upang maiwan ang ilang College Student Councils (CSC) na may mga hindi pa nababayarang obligasyon.

“Seven months, wala pa rin ho na ibabalik. Natural ang mga suppliers, ang mga tumulong sa atin na venues, seven months, hindi pa rin ho nababayaran,” pahayag ni TSU President Dr. Jasper Jay Mendoza. 

Tinalakay ang usapin sa isang pulong ng mga kinauukulang opisina at student leaders matapos maantala ang pagproseso ng nasabing pondo. 

Ayon sa mga pahayag sa pulong, hinati ang ₱1.5 milyon batay sa bilang ng mga atleta ng bawat kolehiyo, kung saan nakalaan ang ₱135,000 hanggang ₱160,000 bawat college.

Ayon sa Finance Committee na pinamumunuan noon ni dating SSC Senator on Finance Kyla Reyes, nakumpleto at naipasa na ang mga kinakailangan, kabilang ang payroll at iba pang dokumento ng mga kolehiyo. May tala rin ng pisikal na pagsusumite ng mga dokumento sa Sports Development and Management Unit (SDMU) noong Hunyo 16, na sinundan ng follow-up noong Hunyo 19.

“We’ve already done our part sa Finance Committee. Inayos na namin lahat ng kailangan ayusin sa requirements, inayos namin lahat ‘yun ng ilang buwan, then nag-pass na kami ng requirements, compiled, sa SDMU,” ani Reyes.

Dagdag pa ni Reyes na sinubukan nilang magpapirma ng log sheet kay SDMU Director Dr. George De Vera bilang tanda na natanggap na ng opisina ang mga dokumento.

“Pero po, ang sagot ni Sir George sa amin 'Na-receive ko na, ipapakuha ko na lang sa clerk ko.' Kaya hindi na namin din natuloy ipapirma ‘yung log sheet.”

Samantala, binanggit ni SDMU Director George De Vera na “As far as I remember, ang sabi ng in-charge sa Finance, okay na lahat ‘yung document.”

Gayunpaman, nang magsagawa ng follow-up sa iba pang tanggapan, hindi umano nakita sa Accounting, Budget, BPA, at Cashiering Office ang mga dokumentong kaugnay ng ₱1.5-milyong request. Dahil dito, nananatiling hindi malinaw kung saan nahinto ang proseso.
“Sobrang tagal na rin po, inabot na po ng 5 months mahigit. Hindi po kami nakakuha ng update sa both po, finance and sa SDMU. Kaya nag-aantay lang po kami nang nag-aantay,” banggit ni dating SSC President, Brixter Millo.

Sa diskusyon, lumitaw na kapwa naging bahagi ng proseso ang Finance Committee at SDMU, habang binigyang-diin din ng mga opisyal na kailangang dumaan sa kaukulang university process ang paghahanda at pagproseso ng mga dokumento para sa sports-related expenses.

Samantala, ang pagkaantala ng pondo ay nag-iwan ng mga gastusing kailangang saluhin ng ilang college governors. Ayon sa mga napag-usapan, may ilang utang sa print shops na umaabot sa ₱80,000 hanggang ₱100,000, bukod pa sa mga bayarin para sa venues at iba pang suppliers.

Kabilang dito ang hindi pa nababayarang bayarin sa College of the Holy Spirit, na ginamit bilang venue para sa isang sports category. 
Binigyang-diin sa pulong na pitong buwan nang hindi nababayaran ang ilang suppliers at venues na naging bahagi ng pagsasagawa ng Intramurals.

Bilang tugon, iminungkahi sa pulong na muling tipunin at ayusin ang mga dokumentong kinakailangan upang maipagpatuloy ang pagproseso ng pondo. Kabilang dito ang mga kopya ng approved budget request, payroll, at iba pang supporting documents na maaaring magsilbing patunay ng naunang pagsusumite.

“Provide the necessary requirements and documents. Then, we will help you facilitate this. We will give you the funds. But provided to complete all documents,” dagdag ni Pres. Mendoza.

Sa pagtatapos ng talakayan, hiniling ang pagtutulungan ng Finance, SDMU, at student regent upang makumpleto ang mga kinakailangan at maipagpatuloy ang proseso ng paglalabas ng pondo.

title: TSU-OSR, SSS seal lived name process for 2026 grad rites; implementation guidelines still pending
author: Trixie L. Galulu
excerpt: The Tarlac State University - Office of the Student Regent (TSU-OSR), in joint representation with the Safe Space Society (SSS), has secured the policy that will allow this year’s graduating students to have their lived names visually and…
body:
The Tarlac State University - Office of the Student Regent (TSU-OSR), in joint representation with the Safe Space Society (SSS), has secured the policy that will allow this year’s graduating students to have their lived names visually and verbally recognized during the 37th Commencement Exercises.

The Office of Gender and Development (OGAD), however, has confirmed that concrete guidelines on its implementation have yet to be finalized.

Formally submitted on July 16, the Petition for the Adoption and Implementation of the Lived Names Process for Graduating Students pushes for acknowledgement of the names that transgender, non-binary, and other LGBTQIA+ students authentically identify with.

In line with the Safe Spaces Act (RA 11313) and Commission on Higher Education (CHED) Memo Order no. 01, s. 2015, the petition also draws from similar policies already implemented at other institutions such as the University of the Philippines (UP), Polytechnic University of the Philippines (PUP), and Far Eastern University (FEU).

Under this, graduates then would be called by their preferred names as they cross the stage, but the request covers only verbal announcements and screen displays, and will not alter official legal documents to keep the process compliant with existing legal standards.

In a Facebook post, the TSU-SSS celebrated the development, considering it not only a name change but a recognition of the dignity, identity, and everyone’s right to be recognized for who they truly are.

“Ito ang patunay na kapag sama-samang sumusugod at lumalaban, may mga guhit na hindi na kailanman mabubura!” the TSU-SSS added.

The OSR echoed similar sentiments, saying: “This breakthrough proves that when student leaders and institutional leaders align on student rights, transformative change occurs. To the Graduating Class of 2026, march proudly into the world as you truly are.”

Both the TSU-SSS and OSR thanked the Offices of Admission and Registration, Student Affairs and Services, the Vice President for Academic Affairs, and the University President for their continued support for the student-led initiative, resulting in another major milestone in the promotion of a more inclusive campus.

Meanwhile, now that the approval has been publicized, TSUians are advised to hold off on submitting their requests until further instructions on the implementation process are released.

Once the details on the guidelines are finalized, graduating students who want to have their lived names during the commencement rites will be asked to pass their information through an official link to be circulated via their respective department group chats.

title: Walang Sisidlang Daing: Paano Magsasalita ang Bayang Kapos sa Hininga?
author: Leanne Chrizelle C. Sarmiento
body:
Tuwing Agosto, kasabay ng paggunita sa ating wika ang panunumbalik ng madilim na langit, ang tila walang katapusang pagbuhos ng ulan, at ang muling pagbisita ng rumaragasang tubig-baha. 

Ang ating wika ay mismong hininga ng ating karanasan. Hinihingal. Kinakapos. Natatapos. Kung marinig man ng langit ang hinaing mo at dasal, may ginhawa.

Hinuhubog ito ng ating kolektibong danas. 

Sapagkat ang karanasan ng Pilipino ay nakasulat na sa bawat salitang may kinalaman sa paghinga—dahil sa bansang ito, ang maging buhay at umiral ay isang araw-araw na pakikipagsapalaran.

Sabi ng ating pambansang bayani, “𝘈𝘯𝘨 𝘩𝘪𝘯𝘥𝘪 𝘮𝘢𝘳𝘶𝘯𝘰𝘯𝘨 𝘮𝘢𝘨𝘮𝘢𝘩𝘢𝘭 𝘴𝘢 𝘴𝘢𝘳𝘪𝘭𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘸𝘪𝘬𝘢 𝘢𝘺 𝘮𝘢𝘴 𝘮𝘢𝘴𝘢𝘩𝘰𝘭 𝘱𝘢 𝘴𝘢 𝘩𝘢𝘺𝘰𝘱 𝘢𝘵 𝘮𝘢𝘭𝘢𝘯𝘴𝘢𝘯𝘨 𝘪𝘴𝘥𝘢.” 

Mahal naman natin ang ating wika. Hindi rin tayo ang hayop. At higit sa lahat, hindi sa atin galing ang lansa. 

𝗣𝗲𝗿𝗼, 𝗯𝗮𝗸𝗶𝘁 𝘁𝗮𝘆𝗼 𝗮𝗻𝗴 𝗸𝗮𝗶𝗹𝗮𝗻𝗴𝗮𝗻𝗴 𝗺𝗮𝗺𝘂𝗵𝗮𝘆 𝗻𝗴 𝗹𝘂𝗯𝗼𝗴 𝘀𝗮 𝘁𝘂𝗯𝗶𝗴𝗮𝗻 𝗸𝘂𝗻𝗴 𝗵𝗶𝗻𝗱𝗶 𝘁𝗮𝘆𝗼 𝗮𝗻𝗴 ‘𝗶𝘀𝗱𝗮’?

Hindi na bago ang sunod-sunod na hagupit ng bagyo tuwing sasapit ang buwan ng Agosto. Hindi na rin nakagugulat ang bahang laging binabantayan sa tuwing bumubuhos ang ulan—ang mga tulo ng tubig sa butas na yero, mga timba at palangganang nakakalat sa sahig upang saluhin ito, at ang nakaugaliang pagtitiis nating mga Pilipino.

Ngunit kasabay ng paghupa ng tubig ang ating ala-ala. 

Ito marahil ang sinasabi nilang panganib ng natapos na delubyo. Aanurin pabalik sa ilog ang galit ng puso, at magiging ga-putik sa labo ang maiiwang hustisya.

Sa mga pahayag ni Malacañang Press Officer Usec., Claire Castro, malinaw na hindi lang sakuna ang kalaban ng mga Pilipino, maging ang sistemang nakakulong sa magagarang bubong ng palasyo.

“𝘏𝘪𝘯𝘥𝘪 𝘬𝘢𝘺𝘢 𝘯𝘨 𝘢𝘵𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘨𝘰𝘣𝘺𝘦𝘳𝘯𝘰 𝘯𝘢 𝘮𝘢𝘨𝘵𝘳𝘢𝘣𝘢𝘩𝘰 𝘯𝘢𝘯𝘨 𝘮𝘢𝘨𝘵𝘳𝘢𝘣𝘢𝘩𝘰, 𝘱𝘦𝘳𝘰 𝘢𝘯𝘨 𝘢𝘵𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘮𝘨𝘢 𝘬𝘢𝘣𝘢𝘣𝘢𝘺𝘢𝘯 𝘢𝘺 𝘱𝘢𝘣𝘢𝘺𝘢 𝘯𝘢𝘯𝘨 𝘱𝘢𝘣𝘢𝘺𝘢. 𝘓𝘢𝘩𝘢𝘵 𝘱𝘰 𝘵𝘢𝘺𝘰 𝘢𝘺 𝘮𝘢𝘨𝘵𝘶𝘭𝘶𝘯𝘨-𝘵𝘶𝘭𝘶𝘯𝘨𝘢𝘯. 𝘓𝘢𝘩𝘢𝘵 𝘱𝘰 𝘵𝘢𝘺𝘰 𝘳𝘪𝘵𝘰 𝘢𝘺 𝘥𝘢𝘱𝘢𝘵 𝘬𝘶𝘮𝘪𝘭𝘰𝘴. 𝘏𝘪𝘯𝘥𝘪 𝘱𝘸𝘦𝘥𝘦𝘯𝘨 𝘯𝘢𝘨𝘬𝘶𝘬𝘶𝘺𝘢-𝘬𝘶𝘺𝘢𝘬𝘰𝘺 𝘭𝘢𝘯𝘨 𝘵𝘢𝘺𝘰 𝘭𝘢𝘨𝘪.”

Sinasabing ang isda ay nahuhuli sa sarili nitong bibig. At sa pagkakataong ito, ang mga nasa taas mismo ang nabibingwit sa sarili nilang dila—ang lansa ng kanilang mga pahayag ay umaalingasaw kasabay ng daloy ng baha.

𝘚𝘢𝘯𝘢𝘺𝘢𝘯 𝘯𝘢 𝘭𝘢𝘯𝘨. 

Sabi nga nila Mang Carlos, isang magsasaka mula sa Concepcion, Tarlac, sanayan na lang. Hindi na bago para sa gaya nila na malunod sa pawis at baha sa gitna ng mga nakadapa’t nasirang pananim. Hindi na rin bago na marinig silang sisihin. 

Gayundin ang walang pagbabago sa Camiling, Tarlac, kung saan ang pinakamahal na 𝘧𝘭𝘰𝘰𝘥 𝘤𝘰𝘯𝘵𝘳𝘰𝘭 𝘱𝘳𝘰𝘫𝘦𝘤𝘵 sa bansa ang siya pang unang sumuko sa agos.

𝗞𝘂𝗻𝗴 𝗮𝗻𝗴 𝗺𝗴𝗮 𝗯𝗮𝗸𝗮𝗹 𝗻𝗮 𝗯𝘂𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝘀𝗮 𝗺𝗶𝗹𝘆𝗼𝗻𝗲𝘀 𝗻𝗴 𝗸𝗮𝗯𝗮𝗻 𝗻𝗴 𝗯𝗮𝘆𝗮𝗻 𝗮𝘆 𝗸𝗮𝘆 𝗱𝗮𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘀𝘂𝗻𝘁𝘂𝗸𝗶𝗻 𝗻𝗴 𝗵𝗮𝗯𝗮𝗴𝗮𝘁, 𝗵𝗶𝗻𝗱𝗶 𝗺𝗼 𝗺𝗮𝘀𝗶𝘀𝗶𝘀𝗶 𝗸𝘂𝗻𝗴 𝗯𝗮𝗸𝗶𝘁 𝗺𝗮𝗽𝗮𝗽𝗮𝗯𝘂𝗻𝘁𝗼𝗻𝗴-𝗵𝗶𝗻𝗶𝗻𝗴𝗮 𝗸𝗮 𝘀𝗮 𝗴𝗼𝗯𝘆𝗲𝗿𝗻𝗼𝗻𝗴 𝗽𝘂𝗿𝗼 𝗽𝗮𝗻𝗴𝗮𝗸𝗼 𝘀𝗮 𝗴𝗶𝘁𝗻𝗮 𝗻𝗴 𝗸𝗮𝗹𝗮𝗺𝗶𝗱𝗮𝗱.

Kumalma man ang bagyo at humupa ang baha, maaamoy mo parin ang lansa sa mga naiwang tubig—siyang mga nilalangaw sa bulsa’t binubusal ng katotohanan sa bibig.

Sa paulit-ulit na mga tagpong ginapos ng kahirapan, siniksik sa ating isipan na lumangoy kasabay ng nakasusulasok na agos. Sa bawat pagtimbol laban sa lantak ng alon, unti-unting namumulikat ang ating kalamnan. Kasabay ng pagbitaw ng katawan, ang pagragasa sa pag-asa ng maginhawang bukas.

𝗞𝗶𝗻𝗮𝗸𝗮𝗽𝗼𝘀 𝗻𝗮 𝘀𝗮 𝗵𝗶𝗻𝗶𝗻𝗴𝗮. 𝗞𝘂𝗻𝗴 𝗵𝗶𝗻𝗱𝗶 𝗵𝗶𝗵𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗼, 𝗯𝗮𝗸𝗮 𝗵𝗶𝗻𝗱𝗶 𝗸𝗮 𝗻𝗮 𝗺𝗮𝗸𝗮-𝗮𝗵𝗼𝗻 𝗽𝗮.

Mali si Usec Castro. Hindi pabaya ang mga Pilipino. Marami tayong ginagawa, at hindi dapat ito ang pangunahing solusyon ng gobyerno. Sa kabila kasi ng paghanga sa 𝘳𝘦𝘴𝘪𝘭𝘪𝘦𝘯𝘤𝘺, kalakip nito ang isang katotohanang mahirap balewalain—ang katatagang ipinagmamalaki natin ay hindi naman tunay na likas. Ito ay may hangganan at wakas.

Higit na sumisidhi ang mga karanasang ito kapag isinasalaysay sa ating sariling wika. 

𝙎𝙖𝙥𝙖𝙜𝙠𝙖𝙩 𝙖𝙣𝙜 𝙁𝙞𝙡𝙞𝙥𝙞𝙣𝙤 𝙖𝙮 𝙝𝙞𝙣𝙙𝙞 𝙡𝙖𝙢𝙖𝙣𝙜 𝙗𝙞𝙣𝙪𝙗𝙪𝙤𝙙 𝙣𝙜 𝙢𝙜𝙖 𝙨𝙖𝙡𝙞𝙩𝙖, 𝙢𝙖𝙮 𝙢𝙜𝙖 𝙠𝙬𝙚𝙣𝙩𝙤𝙣𝙜 𝙋𝙞𝙡𝙞𝙥𝙞𝙣𝙤 𝙣𝙖 𝙥𝙪𝙢𝙪𝙥𝙪𝙠𝙖𝙬 𝙨𝙖 𝙙𝙖𝙢𝙙𝙖𝙢𝙞𝙣𝙜 𝙢𝙖𝙮 𝙙𝙞𝙞𝙣, 𝙡𝙞𝙣𝙖𝙬, 𝙖𝙩 𝙢𝙖𝙮 𝙥𝙞𝙣𝙖𝙜𝙢𝙪𝙢𝙪𝙡𝙖𝙣 𝙣𝙖 𝙨𝙪𝙜𝙖𝙩.

Kaya, kung magwiwika man ngayong Buwan ng Wika, hindi ito upang magmakaawa—kung hindi upang sapilitan silang makinig bago pa tuluyang manahimik ang bayang kinakapos sa hininga. 

*** 
Sa taon-taon na pagkalubog sa tubig-baha, itinuturing na tayong mga kayang mamuhay sa ilalim ng tubig. Kung lubog na sa baha, mahirap na ang huminga—paano pa kaya ang magsalita?

Ang isda raw ay nahuhuli sa sariling bibig, pero ang mga Pilipino’y mahuhuli ng agos kung hindi niyo maririnig. 

Kaya atin itong bigkasing sabay-sabay nang mahuli naman ng mga nasa itaas ang hinaing nating mga nasa laylayan: 𝘏𝘪𝘯𝘥𝘪 𝘬𝘢𝘮𝘪 𝘪𝘴𝘥𝘢!

title: TSU stude orgs, pubs stand in solidarity with Capas Aetas, residents vs. PAF’s “danger zone” restrictions
author: Andrei P. Opeña
excerpt: Various recognized student organizations and publications of Tarlac State University (TSU) have stood in solidarity with indigenous peoples (IPs) and residents of Capas, Tarlac against the strict military measures imposed by the…
body:
Various recognized student organizations and publications of Tarlac State University (TSU) have stood in solidarity with indigenous peoples (IPs) and residents of Capas, Tarlac against the strict military measures imposed by the Philippine Air Force (PAF) inside five barangays within the town, which it labeled as “danger zone.”

This comes after thousands of residents and IPs from the barangays, including Maruglo, Bueno, O'Donnell, Sta. Juliana, and Sta. Lucia, have collectively voiced their opposition to the said measures on the streets of Sitio Calanat, Barangay O'Donnell, Capas, Tarlac on July 14 to seek immediate resolutions from the PAF.

The organizations, which include the Supreme Student Council (SSC), Safe Space Society (SSS), Kaya Natin Youth - TSU Chapter (KNY-TSU), the Educators’ Gazette, and The Bureaucrat, aired their strong condemnation against the PAF’s efforts to militarize the communities, deeming it an aggressive maneuver of land-grabbing.

“Ang pagbansag sa kanilang mga pamayanan bilang mga “danger zone” upang bigyang-tuwid ang pagpapalayas at harasment ay isang marahas na taktika ng pang-aagaw ng lupa,” the TSU-SSC wrote in a statement relased on Facebook.

It added that the military and the fascist state are being utilized as instruments to displace IPs and pave the way for giant projects that prioritize foreign interests over the welfare of local Filipino citizens.

In light of this, the council called for the immediate cessation of PAF’s militarization, harassment, and intimidation, and the full recognition of the rights of IPs and the residents to their ancestral domains.

“Hindi mananatiling tahimik ang mga iskolar ng bayan habang ang ating mga karatig-komunidad sa Tarlac ay pinagkakaitan ng kanilang karapatan sa sariling lupa at karapatang mamuhay,” SSC noted.

KNY-TSU echoed similar sentiments, calling for the lifting of all the oppressive restrictions imposed by the PAF upon the communities and honoring their members’ rights as provided in the Constitution and existing human rights laws.

As a socio-political student organization advocating for ethical leadership and good governance, the group also called on government agencies to inquire into the communities’ long-standing complaints.

“The people of Capas are not enemies of the State. They are fellow Filipinos as well who deserve their rights to be protected—not oppressed. Their ancestral territories are not war trophies, nor are their lives bargaining chips to institutionalized violence,” it highlighted.

The TSU-SSS, meanwhile, in a separate statement, stated that the fight for safe spaces is also a fight for the dignity, rights, and land that indigenous peoples have long held and called home.

“Dahil ang ligtas na espasyo ay hindi lamang dapat ipinaglalaban sa loob ng pamantasan. Ipinaglalaban din ito sa bawat komunidad kung saan may mga taong patuloy na inaagawan ng boses at karapatan,” the statement read.

On the other hand, the Educators’ Gazette, official publication of the College of Education (CoEd), said that this issue is not only a land dispute but a “struggle for dignity, livelihood, and the recognition of rights that communities have long fought to protect.”

The publication also highlighted the need for the concerns of the affected communities to be “heard, investigated, and addressed through dialogue rather than force,” thus also urging concerned government agencies to immediately act and provide a rights-based resolution to the issue.

“The struggle for ancestral lands is ultimately a struggle for justice. And justice cannot exist where the voices of the people are ignored,” it concluded.

Meanwhile, The Bureaucrat, official publication of the College of Public Administration and Governance (CPAG), criticized protocols and projects that prioritize the interests of the state and giant companies towards their so-called “development.”

“Walang pag-unlad na makatarungan kung nagsisimula ito sa pagpapalayas, pananakot, at pagyapak sa karapatan ng mga unang tagapag-alaga ng mga lupaing ito,” the publication emphasized, calling for the preservation of ancestral lands, rejection of imperialist exploitation Philippine natural resources, and an end to development aggression.

Apart from the above organizations, the Alliance of Concerned Students (ACS) - TSU and Sandigan - TSU also expressed their support for the communities’ assertion of their rights, arguing that militarization and fascism should never be used to detrimentally affect local citizens only to uphold oppressive foreign interests.

title: Pagbaha, nagtulak sa mga pamilya na lumikas sa Paniqui, Tarlac
author: Alyssa L. Cerezo
excerpt: ‎Dahil sa Habagat, ilang komunidad sa Paniqui, Tarlac ang napilitang lumikas patungo sa Balaoang National High School (BNHS) matapos tumaas ang tubig sa mga bahagi ng Barangay Aduas at Balaoang noong Linggo, Agosto 30.
body:
‎Dahil sa Habagat, ilang komunidad sa Paniqui, Tarlac ang napilitang lumikas patungo sa Balaoang National High School (BNHS) matapos tumaas ang tubig sa mga bahagi ng Barangay Aduas at Balaoang noong Linggo, Agosto 30.
‎
‎Sa Purok Pangasinan, Barangay Aduas, iniulat ng isang residente na nagsimulang tumaas ang tubig-baha bandang alas-8:30 ng gabi noong Sabado, Agosto 29. Bagama’t bahagyang bumaba ito bandang alas-10 ng gabi, muli itong tumaas pagsapit ng ala-1 hanggang alas-3 ng madaling-araw noong Linggo. Hindi umano inaasahan ng mga residente ang biglaang pagtaas ng tubig, na umabot sa lagpas-tuhod sa ilang bahagi ng lugar, kaya napilitan ang ilan na humanap ng mas ligtas na matutuluyan.
‎
‎Bandang alas-8 ng gabi noong Sabado, nagtungo rin umano sa lugar ang lokal na pamahalaan, kabilang ang alkalde, upang magbigay ng tulong sa mga residente. Ayon sa ulat, bumalik ang mga ito bandang alas-5 ng madaling-araw upang ipagpatuloy ang pagtugon sa mga apektadong pamilya.
‎
‎Humigit-kumulang 200 pamilya ang naiulat na naapektuhan sa lugar; ang ilan ay piniling lumikas habang ang iba naman ay nanatili upang bantayan ang kanilang mga tahanan at ari-arian. Gayunpaman, sinabi ng isang residenteng nagngangalang Ruth Aquino na, “Wala nang natira, dahil sobrang taas at hindi inaasahan ang baha.”
‎
‎Samantala, iniulat ng mga residente sa Core Balaoang na umabot sa lagpas-tuhod ang tubig-baha, at sa ilang bahagi ng mga kalsada ay umabot pa ito hanggang sa katawan (torso) bandang alas-3:00 ng madaling-araw ng Linggo. Tumulong ang mga opisyal ng barangay sa mga apektadong residente sa pamamagitan ng pagbibigay ng transportasyon at iba pang uri ng tulong.
‎
‎Sinimulan ng lokal na pamahalaan ng Paniqui ang relief operations noong madaling-araw ng Linggo, bandang alas-5:00 ng umaga, sa pamamagitan ng pagbibigay ng mga pangunahing pangangailangan. Gayunpaman, may ilang pamilya—kabilang ang mga sanggol—na hindi nakatanggap ng relief goods at napilitang matulog sa basang karton.
‎
‎Nagdulot din ang pagbaha ng pagsasara ng kalsada sa Rang-Ayan Bridge matapos ma-trap ang mga trak at iba pang mabibigat na sasakyan habang sinusubukang tumawid. Naiulat na nakadaan pa rin ang mga magagaan na sasakyan, tulad ng mga motorsiklo at tricycle, habang naglagay naman ng mga checkpoint sa mga kalapit na kalsadang patungo sa Pangasinan at Camiling. Bandang alas-6:30 ng gabi, naiulat na bumalik na sa normal ang antas ng tubig sa Rang-Ayan Bridge.
‎
‎Gayunpaman, patuloy pa ring bumabangon ang mga residente sa mga apektadong komunidad mula sa epekto ng pagbaha, kung saan ang ilan ay nangangailangan pa rin ng mga pangunahing pangangailangan at tulong.

title: Kasing-Lagkit at Kasing-Tamis: Ang Mahabang Kwento ng Paskong Pinoy
author: Alelie Jade J. Mallari
excerpt: Hindi lamang sa mga nakasabit na parol o himig ng mga batang nagsisikantahan maaaninag ang pagsapit ng Pasko.
body:
Hindi lamang sa mga nakasabit na parol o himig ng mga batang nagsisikantahan maaaninag ang pagsapit ng Pasko. 

Marahil, kung tatahakin mo ang bawat kalsada’t lansangan, mababatid mo na nanunuot na sa simoy ng malamig na hangin ang Pasko bago pa man ito tuluyang sumapit. Sa bawat sulok, may kung anong unti-unting nagbabago. Mas nagiging madalas ang mga bahid ng pula, berde’t puti sa mga 𝘤𝘰𝘮𝘮𝘦𝘳𝘤𝘪𝘢𝘭 at magasin. Mas kumokonti ang mga sangkap na nabibili para sa mga 𝘧𝘳𝘶𝘪𝘵 𝘴𝘢𝘭𝘢𝘥 at 𝘴𝘱𝘢𝘨𝘩𝘦𝘵𝘵𝘪. Mas tumatapang ang amoy ng mga keso’t usok na sumisingaw mula sa pugon kung saan tila namamahay ang sarap ng bibingka’t puto bumbong.

At bago pa man natin mapansin, ika nga nila—Pasko na naman!

Unti-unti itong sumisiksik sa pagitan ng mga karaniwang araw. Sa mga awitin ni Jose Mari Chan at Mariah Carey na paulit-ulit na umaalingawngaw mula sa mga tindahan, sa mga pabatid sa lahat ng 𝘤𝘩𝘢𝘯𝘯𝘦𝘭 ng balita sa mga natitirang araw bago ang Pasko, at sa mga mukha ni 𝘚𝘢𝘯𝘵𝘢 𝘊𝘭𝘢𝘶𝘴 na nakapaskil sa halos lahat ng pintuan.

Ganito sinusukat ang pagdating ng kapaskuhan sa Pilipinas—hindi mula sa mga numero’t pahina ng kalendaryo, kundi sa mga maliliit na pagbabagong nagiging sangkap para sa isang malasang Pasko.

𝗣𝗮𝘀𝗸𝗼 𝗻𝗮 𝗡𝗮𝗺-𝗻𝗮𝗺!

Hindi minamadali ang tunay na sarap. 

Tulad ng Pirurutong na kailangan ibabad nang matagal sa tubig upang palabasin ang malambot na tekstura at matingkad na kulay lila nito. Sa kulturang Pilipino, ang pagdiriwang sa pasko ay hindi lamang isang kaganapan na nangyayari sa isang iglap, kundi isang mahaba at dahan-dahan na paghubog—isang tradisyon na sumisibol mula Setyembre hanggang Disyembre. 

Ang 𝘉𝘦𝘳 𝘔𝘰𝘯𝘵𝘩𝘴 ay ang ating sariling proseso ng pagbabad. Hindi sa tubig, kundi sa pananabik sa isang pagdiriwang na tinuturing nating mga Pilipino na pinaka perpektong kanlungan ng sigla at pagmamahal. 

At sa pananabik na ito, dahan-dahang nabubuo ang ang liwanag ng mga parol, sumusulpot ang mga batang may dala-dalang mga basyong bote ng 𝘴𝘰𝘧𝘵𝘥𝘳𝘪𝘯𝘬𝘴 na may nilalamang maliliit na bato, bahay sa bahay ang pag-awit ng 𝘤𝘢𝘳𝘰𝘭𝘪𝘯𝘨. At dumarating na rin ang lumalakad na halimuyak ng ginagawang puto bumbong sa tabing kanto tuwing kailaliman ng gabi. Patunay na pagpatak pa lamang ng Setyembre ay tunay ngang buhay na ang diwa ng Pasko.

Itinuturing ang Pilipinas bilang bansang mayroong pinaka mahabang pagdiriwang ng pasko. Hindi lamang natin sinusukat sa isang petsa ang kasiyahan, dahil mula pa lamang sa paghihintay ay ibinubuhos na natin ang ating puso at sigla sa mga kaganapan. 

Sa halip na maghintay nang walang kabuluhan, binibigyang lasa na natin ang mismong proseso ng pag-aabang, dahil naiintindihan natin na ang mga magagandang bagay ay nangangailangan ng panahon— mas masarap maranasan kapag pinalipas nang matagal.

Katulad ng puto bumbong, ang pagbabad nito sa tubig ay ang tanging prosesong sumisigurado na masarap ang kinalabasan nito. Sa parehong paraan, ang tatlong buwan na paghahanda natin sa pasko ay siyang nagbibigay ng kakaibang lasa sa paskong Pilipino.

Kailanman hindi natin itinuring na nakakayamot ang paghihintay rito, sa halip, ito ay ang nagtuturing sikretong sangkap natin sa isang maligaya, at masiglang pasko.

Dahil kapag naiahon na sa paghihintay ang mga Pilipino, dito na lilitaw ang tunay na kagandahan ng ating pagkatao. Nagiging malambot ang pusong tumigas bunsod sa mga ibinigay na pagsubok ng mga naunang buwan. Ngayo’y handang handang isalang sa init ng pagmamahal tuwing kapaskuhan. 

𝗕𝘂𝗱𝗯𝗼𝗱 𝗻𝗴 𝗨𝗯𝗼𝗱 𝗻𝗮 𝗣𝗮𝗴𝗺𝗮𝗺𝗮𝗵𝗮𝗹

          Habang nakasalang ang bumbong sa umuusok na lansungan, kumakawala ang pinakamayamang halimuyak nito na tila bang nagbibigay sa atin ng lansangan patungo sa paskong kay sarap salubungin—lalo na kapag hinaluan ng init ng pagmamahalan sa ilalim ng ating sari sariling mga bubong.

            At tuwing ang halimuyak na ito ay sumusuot sa ating mga ilong, ang pasko ay hindi na lamang petsa na basta basta lamang nakaguhit sa kalendaryo—kundi, isang paalala na ang tunay na tamis ng pasko ay ang pag-alam na ang mahabang panahon ng ating pagbabad sa paghihintay ay hindi nasayang, bagkus, isang linamnam na kay sarap namnamin.
           
          Kada paikot ng monito monita, sa mga simpleng twalya’t tasang paulit-ulit ma’y palaging may bitbit na pag-alala, at sa mga bukas na palad na inilalahad sa mga ninong at ninang, hindi lamang napupuno ang ating mga kamay sa pagtanggap, kundi dahan-dahang rin humuhubog sa ating puso ang natutuhang pagpapahalaga, pagpapasalamat, at pagmamahal.

          Bawat pagkurap ng nakasinding parol sa mga kalsada ay siyang nagtataboy sa anino na nasisilayan ng ating mga mata—nagpapaalala na sa huling yugto ng taon ay laging may nakalaang ginhawa at saya.

      Marahil, ito siguro ang lihim kung bakit maagang gumigising at matagal humihinga ang pasko sa ating bansa. Dahil sa loob ng tatlong daan at animnapu’t araw, pasan natin ang samu’t saring bigat at mga tahimik na dusa, kaya nama’y ang apat na buwang pagdiriwang ay nagsisilbing takasan kung saan panandaliang nalilimot ang sugat ng kahapon.

𝗣𝗮𝗻𝗹𝗮𝘀𝗮𝗻𝗴 𝗣𝗶𝗻𝗼𝘆

	Hindi nagtatapos sa paglabas ng puto bumbong mula sa kawayan ang paghahanda nito. Sapagkat bago ito tuluyang ihain, nilalagyan pa ito ng mga pang-ibabaw na siyang nagbibigay ng karagdagang kulay at linamnam—ang nilusaw na mantikilya, mala-kayumangging asukal, at kinudkod na niyog. 

Marahil, sa unang tingin ay hindi naman ganoon kalaki ang naidudulot ng mga ito. May sariling tamis na nga naman ang pirurutong na bagong ahon mula sa kawayan—ekstra na lamang ang linamnam na dala ng lusaw na mantikilya at asukal. Hindi na rin naman kailangang gamitin ang mga kinudkod na niyog bilang palamuti sa puto bumbong. Subalit sa kabila ng ito, hindi maitatanggi na ang mga maliliit na bagay na gaya ng mga pang-ibabaw na ito ang siyang nagbibigay rito ng lasa na madaling makilala at matawag na 𝘢𝘵𝘪𝘯.

	Hindi mo mahahanap ang halina at tamis ng puto bumbong sa 𝘨𝘪𝘯𝘨𝘦𝘳𝘣𝘳𝘦𝘢𝘥 ng mga Amerikano. Iba rin ang lambot at lagkit ng 𝘮𝘰𝘤𝘩𝘪 ng mga Hapon. Hindi mo magagawang iluto ang puto bumbong gamit ang kasangkapan na para sa gingerbread. Hindi mo rin magagamit ang lansungan na para sa puto bumbong upang makuha ang malambot at malagkit na pagkayari ng 𝘮𝘰𝘤𝘩𝘪. 

	Hindi kailangang magkakatulad ang mga panimpla at pang-ibabaw ng bawat panghimagas upang matawag itong malasa. Sa halip, ang mga sari-sariling sangkap at proseso ng paghahanda ng mga ito ay ang siyang nagbibigay sa mga ito ng kanilang sariling diwa at pagkakakilanlan. 

	Ganoon din ang pasko. Ipinagdiriwang ito sa iba’t ibang panig ng mundo, ngunit bawat kultura ay may sari-sariling paraan ng paglalagay ng lasa rito. Sa Paskong Pilipino, hindi lamang iisang tradisyon ang itinuturing sangkap upang matawag itong 𝘢𝘵𝘪𝘯. Gaya ng mga pang-ibabaw sa puto bumbong, yari ang Paskong Pilipino sa pinagsama-samang katas ng kulturang Pilipino gaya paggawa ng parol, Simbang Gabi, awiting pamasko, 𝘤𝘢𝘳𝘰𝘭𝘪𝘯𝘨, maagang paghahanda, at mga hapag na pinagsasaluhan tuwing 𝘯𝘰𝘤𝘩𝘦 𝘣𝘶𝘦𝘯𝘢.

	Ngunit tulad ng puto bumbong, hindi rin natatapos ang Pasko sa sandaling ito’y maihain at maubos. 

	Nananatiling nakasabit ang mga parol sa harap ng mga tahanan. Tuwing gabi, binubuhay pa rin ng mga makukulay na ilaw ang bubong ng bawat bahay. Iniinit muli ang mga tirang pagkain na pinagsaluhan noong 𝘯𝘰𝘤𝘩𝘦 𝘣𝘶𝘦𝘯𝘢. Minsan, maririnig pa rin ang halinghing ng 𝘈𝘭𝘭 𝘐 𝘸𝘢𝘯𝘵 𝘧𝘰𝘳 𝘊𝘩𝘳𝘪𝘴𝘵𝘮𝘢𝘴 sa mga tindahan. At higit sa lahat, tuloy tuloy pa rin ang pagsasama-sama ng bawat pamilya hanggang sumapit ang Bagong Taon.

	Gaya ng puto bumbong na dumaan sa pagbababad, pagpapasingaw, at nilagyan ng asukal, lusaw na mantikilya, at kinayod na niyog, ang Pasko ay inihahain rin upang maubos—𝘮𝘢𝘵𝘢𝘱𝘰𝘴. Ngunit dala ng kapanabikan ng bawat Pilipino, ang lasa ng Pasko ay nananatili pa rin sa dila ng mga tao. 

Dahil oo nga naman, sabagay, mayroong mga ilang bagay na mas masarap namnamin kapag hindi minamadaling matapos.

title: TSU welcomes first visually impaired students, pushes for more inclusive education
author: Andrei P. Opeña
excerpt: In line with its ongoing efforts to champion a more inclusive tertiary education, Tarlac State University (TSU) formally welcomed its first two visually impaired students Marvin David Gamasa, 20, and Andrie Helric Pangilinan, 18, at the…
body:
In line with its ongoing efforts to champion a more inclusive tertiary education, Tarlac State University (TSU) formally welcomed its first two visually impaired students Marvin David Gamasa, 20, and Andrie Helric Pangilinan, 18, at the Office of the University President (OUP), July 10.

Both students qualified for the university’s Differently-Abled Individuals Scholarship Program, which granted them 7,000 pesos each for book allowance and stipend for the first semester of academic year 2026–2027.

Gamasa, an honor student at Sto. Cristo Integrated School who plans to take up a Bachelor of Secondary Education major in English degree at TSU, expressed his gratitude to the university for welcoming him and Pangilinan as its first visually impaired student pioneers.

“Our sincerest gratitude to our University President, Dr. Jasper Jay N. Mendoza, and the TSU administration for your warm welcome and firm commitment to inclusive education. Through the DALAN Framework and the RISE FORWARD roadmap, we are highly inspired to excel and contribute to our university community,” he wrote in a Facebook post. 

During an interview with the TSU - Office of Public Affairs (OPA), Gamasa shared that instead of being labeled as a “Person with Disability”, he prefers to be referred to as a “Person with Dreams” who wants to inspire other students through words and music.

“Feeling ko po mas magiging malaya ako rito at ma-e-explore ang creativity compared to noong elementary ako, lakasan lang po ng loob,” he added, considering TSU a safe space where he can showcase and nurture his skills, like singing and braille reading.

Despite his disability, Gamasa said that he does not need special treatment, only reasonable accommodations.

“As a Person with Dreams, I look forward to maximizing reasonable accommodations and proving that digital proficiency is a powerful equalizer in higher education,” he stated.

Meanwhile, Pangilinan, an award-winning Paralympic athlete who is pursuing a Bachelor of Arts in Communication degree at TSU, said that his admission to the university represented not only a personal achievement but a victory shared with other differently-abled students, especially his fellow blind and visually impaired individuals.

“Hindi ko po ito pangarap para sa sarili ko kundi para sa mga katulad ko pong differently-abled students, lalo na po sa mga fellow blind and visually impaired students,” he noted.

TSU President Dr. Jasper Jay Mendoza said that it is one of his visions to build an inclusive university that can cater to all students, including differently-abled and marginalized students, an initiative he has pursued since he was still dean of the College of Education (COEd).

He also expressed his desire to hire Gamasa to teach at TSU as soon as he graduates and passes the licensure exam as the university sets its sights on opening a Bachelor of Special Needs Education (BSNEd) program soon to empower more students with special needs.
“You would be the first blind teacher at TSU,” Mendoza told Gamasa.

To assist the students in their studies, Head of the International, Differently-Abled, Indigenous, and Marginalized Student Services (IDIMSS) Mr. Allan Santos said that they are using Non-Visual Desktop Access (NVDA) software. 

He added that their office is maximizing all efforts to improve the welfare and inclusive learning of the blind students, who will be allowed to stay at the IDIMSS office to rest and print documents essential for learning.

Gamasa and Pangilinan’s admission to TSU marks another major milestone in the university’s cause for inclusivity after its partnership with an Australian firm called Focus Bear that developed digital support systems for neurodivergent students and with the Kakamay Movement, which aims to break communication barriers by promoting Filipino Sign Language (FSL) toward making the university deaf-ready.

title: ‘Resilience was the only way’: COEd valedictorians honor persistence, urge co-grads to keep moving forward
author: Andrei P. Opeña
excerpt: A testament to grit that endured even when the world came to a halt, 1,065 graduates from the College of Education (COED) marched down the aisle to claim their hard-earned diplomas on the third day of the 37th Commencement Exercises at…
body:
A testament to grit that endured even when the world came to a halt, 1,065 graduates from the College of Education (COED) marched down the aisle to claim their hard-earned diplomas on the third day of the 37th Commencement Exercises at the University Gymnasium, July 30.

Anchored on the theme “TSU GRADUATES: A.C.H.I.E.V.E.-ing Excellence in Higher Education, Upholding Truth, Unifying for Nation-Building, and Serving the People with Compassion,” the ceremony celebrated both undergraduate achievers and post-graduate scholars stepping into the professional field.

Leading the class, Joyce Anne D. Polido, Bachelor of Elementary Education (BEED) graduate and hailed batch valedictorian, delivered the valedictory address centered on grit and raw gratitude, describing their walk across the stage as proof of survival.
“This graduation serves as evidence—not just for four years, but for the years that taught us how to keep moving when the world stopped,” Polido shared.

“Resilience is never a choice; it was the only way to keep our dreams alive,” she added. 

Polido further moved the audience as she dedicated her triumph to her parents, reflecting on the profound duty of carrying forward the opportunities that her family was once denied.

“Anong karapatan kong tumigil kung ang mga magulang ko ay hindi nagkaroon ng pagkakataong magsimula?” she declared.
Meanwhile, guest speaker Hon. Tolentino G. Aquino, Department of Education Region I Director, reminded the new educators that impactful teaching begins by meeting people from where they are.

“Ang tunay na mahusay na guro ay marunong tumugon sa konteksto ng kanyang komunidad,” Aquino emphasized, encouraging the batch to stay patient in their calling.

“Ang maliit na hakbang ay nagdudulot ng pangmatagalang pagbabago.,” he added.

On the other hand, leading the afternoon session, Shenayah Loise P. Catacutan, a Bachelor of Secondary Education (BSEd) Major in English magna cum laude graduate, reflected on how life and the people around her became the reason the deadlines she had secretly set for herself were extended, enabling her to reach and become who she is today.

“But one thing I will never regret, it is making it to 22 because every extra year gave me another chance to know someone I couldn't even imagine when I was thirteen,” she stated.

“Because although I kept saying 20 was my last call, deep inside in my heart, there was always a quieter voice—a voice that wanted to know what 21, 22 looked like, a voice that wanted to blow another birthday candle, a voice that wanted to take one more exam, to teach one more class, to meet one more student, and to witness one more sunrise,” the valedictorian added.

Drawing inspiration from her own experiences, she reminded her fellow graduates to “keep moving forward, there is so much life beyond the age you thought could be your last.”

Meanwhile, commencement speaker and guest of honor Hon. Jennie V. Jocson, Executive Director of the Teacher Education Council Secretariat reminded the graduates to do their best to contribute toward the betterment of the country which is currently facing challenges in the education sector.

“Gamitin ang knowledge, ang talents, ang passion in advancing meaningful change and helping build a stronger, more inclusive nation,” she noted.

“Hindi sapat na magturo lamang kayo ng nasa lesson plan. Teach your learners to seek truth in a world where misinformation spreads faster than facts, teach them to ask questions, to think critically, but also to listen with respect,” she added.

- Master in Education Management - 3
- Doctor in Industrial Education Management - 1

title: Landbank-Tarlac educates TSUians on digital conversion in 2-day orientation
author: Joshua Adrian N. Castro
excerpt: Eyeing convenient and efficient transactions, the Landbank of the Philippines (LBP) Tarlac Branch enlightened students from various colleges and organizations in Tarlac State University (TSU) in a 2-day orientation about its Cash-Lite…
body:
Eyeing convenient and efficient transactions, the Landbank of the Philippines (LBP) Tarlac Branch enlightened students from various colleges and organizations in Tarlac State University (TSU) in a 2-day orientation about its Cash-Lite Campus Program, held at the Student Center in Lucinda Campus, July 8 and July 9. 

The orientation comes after LBP Tarlac and TSU signed a memorandum of agreement (MOA) on June 30, which marked the onset of their partnership to provide a more secure and accessible digital payment system through cash-lite, an initiative to promote a cashless economy. 

Vice President and Branch Head of Landbank-Tarlac, Maila Veronica P. Co began the orientation by sharing her beginnings with marketing e-banking facilities to government units back in 2012. 

Initially, she was not paid much attention to by people, but those who did eventually reaped the benefits when the global pandemic hit.
“These government units that have an existing e-banking facility with us—sila ‘yung naging komportable,” she stated. 
“And two years ago [was] when we started ‘yung ating business relationship ni Landbank at saka si TSU,” Co added.

Now, for TSU, advancement in financial transactions is within reach through the Cash-Lite Campus Program, which will make cash flow inside the institution more effortless, trackable, and interconnected.

“Halimbawa estudyante ka, magbabayad ka ng tuition. You will do it electronically using the link disc portal,” Co explained. She further shared that in order for the ecosystem to fully manifest, it is best if all students participate in digital banking.  

Highlighting the importance of cybersecurity, the orientation also educated attendees on how they can protect themselves from scammers, phishing, and manipulative tactics by safeguarding their personal details from strangers, avoiding overexposure on social media, and evaluating the legitimacy of websites and messages.

“Information security starts with awareness... And awareness starts with you,” Co stated emphasizing how being vigilant and prudent is key in ensuring a safe digital citizenship is maintained. 

Meanwhile, in an interview, Customer Associate of Landbank, Irish M. Lactaotao stated that the main goal of the Cash-Lite Program is for it to be inclusive among students. She also mentioned Landbank Piso Plus, which can be used when paying for the university’s shuttle system and canteen—ensuring convenience and safety. 

“Itong ginagawa naming info drive, sana makatulong na i-share nila ‘yung knowledge na nakuha nila dito sa ibang tao, sa parents nila—na pwede rin silang mag-open ng account nila through [their] phone,” Lactaotao remarked. 

The orientation concluded after the students were assisted in registering for their Landbank Piso Plus account using the official Landbank Mobile Banking App.

Future orientations are also expected to be held soon on the Main and San Isidro campuses.

title: Avon Ang kinondena ang red-tagging, HB 2697 sa Cinemamamayan 2026
author: John Hermie M. Sarceda
excerpt: Binatikos ni Mx. Avon Ang, pambansang koordineytor ng Altermidya, ang red-tagging bilang sadyang paraan ng pagligaw-atensyon laban sa mga mamamahayag ng bansa,
body:
Binatikos ni Mx. Avon Ang, pambansang koordineytor ng Altermidya, ang red-tagging bilang sadyang paraan ng pagligaw-atensyon laban sa mga mamamahayag ng bansa, kasabay ng muling pagtutol niya sa House Bill 2697 o ang panukalang Anti-Fake News and Digital Disinformation Act, na aniya’y hindi pinananagot ang social media, mga dambuhalang teknolohiya, at artificial intelligence (AI) kahit patuloy na lumalaki ang banta ng disimpormasyong dulot nito.

Sinabi ito ni Ang bilang unang tagapagsalita sa Cinemamamayan 2026, isang workshop na idinaos ng Provincial Human Rights Office - Tarlac sa Old SP Hall, Tarlac Capitol, kung saan dumalo ang iba't ibang student publications at media organizations.

“Hanggang gobyerno ang magsasabi ng totoo, magiging kalokohan ang batas,” pahayag ni Ang, tungkol sa HB 2697.

Ayon kay Ang, hindi lamang pananakot ang red-tagging kundi isang paraan ng pagligaw-atensyon na direktang nagbabanta sa buhay, seguridad, at kalayaan ng mga mamamahayag, kung saan kadalasang ginagamit upang baliktarin ang lehitimong pag-uulat bilang “pagpopondo sa terorismo.”

Binanggit ni Ang ang kaso ni Frenchie Mae Cumpio, isang broadcast journalist na hanggang ngayo’y hindi pa nakakalaya, bilang babala laban sa mga pagtatangkang gawing presedente ang ganitong mga insidente.

Bukod sa direktang banta, itinuro rin ni Ang ang lumalalim na “chilling effect” sa industriya ng midya, kung saan lalong dumadami ang mga mamamahayag na nagsa-self-censor dahil sa takot na maatake, limitadong akses sa impormasyon, at labis na pag-iingat sa kanilang pag-uulat.

Inilagay ni Ang ang HB 2697 sa mas malawak na pattern ng mga batas na aniya'y unti-unting humihigpit sa kalayaan ng pamamahayag sa Pilipinas, kasama ang Anti-Terrorism Law, Libel and Cyber Crime Prevention Law, at ang SIM Registration Act.

Higit pa rito, hinamon ni Ang ang mga campus publication at ibang mamamahayag na mas pagtibayin ang kolaborasyon sa hanay ng midya, mula sa alternative media, lokal na peryodista, hanggang sa mga student publication, bilang tugon sa lumalaking banta ng “engineered”na disimpormasyon.

Bilang halimbawa ng epektibong kolaborasyon, ikinuwento ni Ang ang kanilang dokumentaryo hinggil sa isyu ng pagmimina sa Nueva Vizcaya, kung saan bumalik sila sa mga apektadong komunidad upang kumuha ng puna at pinalabas pa ang mga kaparehong dokumentaryo mula sa ibang lugar na isang hakbang, aniya, na nagpapakita na hindi nakahiwalay ang bawat isyu, kabilang na ang Pax Silica sa Capas, Tarlac.

Hinikayat din ni Ang ang mga campus publication na magtatag ng sarili nilang feedback mechanisms tulad ng room-to-room na pakikipag-ugnayan sa mga estudyante, dahil base sa kanya, mas nadarama ng mga mag-aaral ang halaga ng isang publikasyon kapag sila mismo ay bahagi ng prosesong ito.

“Solidaridad. Kolaborasyon,” ang kanyang pagdidiin bilang pagtatapos ng kanyang talumpati.

Sa kabilang banda, binigyang-diin ni Direk JL Burgos, nanalo sa FAMAS bilang Best Picture sa kanyang dokyumentaryong tungkol sa kanyang nawawalang aktibistang kapatid na si Jonas Burgos, na ang human rights film ay “pelikula ng mamamayan,” hindi lamang mga estadistika o bilang ng mga napatay o nadukot, kundi kwento ng aktwal na karanasan at aspirasyon ng mga tao.

Binanggit din ni Burgos na ang isang artist, dating tinatawag na "craftsman," ay nagsisilbi sa bayan kung saan inuuna lagi ang tanong na "Para kanino?" sa paggawa ng isang pelikulang pang masa. 

Sinabi rin niya na mahalaga ang lalim ng research bago mag-shoot, upang maiwasan ang tinatawag na “poverty porn,” at dapat na alam ng mismong storyteller kung sino ang kanyang tunay na tinutungtungan.

title: Bridging the Bloodline: Higit sa Monopolyo, Sulong Tarlakenyo!
author: Kate Aira L. Mendoza
excerpt: Hindi lamang semento at bakal ang nasubok ng gumuho ang mga pangunahing tulay sa Tarlac sa gitna ng nagdaang mga pagbaha.
body:
Hindi lamang semento at bakal ang nasubok ng gumuho ang mga pangunahing tulay sa Tarlac sa gitna ng nagdaang mga pagbaha. Kasabay ng pagkalubog ng mga kalsada, pagkaantala ng biyahe, pagkaparalisa ng buhay at kabuhayan ng mga ordinaryong mamamayan, muling nabuksan ang diskurso sa tibay ng ating pampublikong estraktura at ang pamamahala sa likod nito.

𝗠𝗮𝘆 𝗺𝗮𝗹𝗮𝗹𝗶𝗺 𝗻𝗮 𝗽𝗮𝗴𝗸𝗮𝗸𝗮𝗵𝗮𝗹𝗶𝗻𝘁𝘂𝗹𝗮𝗱 𝗮𝗻𝗴 𝗺𝗴𝗮 𝗯𝘂𝗺𝗮𝗴𝘀𝗮𝗸 𝗻𝗮 𝘁𝘂𝗹𝗮𝘆 𝘀𝗮 𝘂𝗺𝗶𝗶𝗿𝗮𝗹 𝗻𝗮 𝘀𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗺𝗮 𝗻𝗴 𝗺𝗴𝗮 𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗮𝘀𝘁𝗶𝘆𝗮𝗻𝗴 𝗽𝗼𝗹𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗸𝗮𝗹 𝘀𝗮 𝗹𝗮𝗹𝗮𝘄𝗶𝗴𝗮𝗻 𝗻𝗴 𝗧𝗮𝗿𝗹𝗮𝗰.

Sa loob ng maraming dekada, tila naging tradisyon na ang pagpapasalin-salin ng katungkulan sa iisang angkan. Sa sistemang ito, ang kapangyarihan ay iisa ang ruta—iisang linya ng dugo na nag-uugnay sa yaman ng nakaraan at kontrol sa kinabukasan ng iilang paksyon. 

Base sa pananaliksik ng Ateneo School of Government (ASoG), ang ganitong sistema ay isang 𝘱𝘰𝘭𝘪𝘵𝘪𝘤𝘢𝘭 𝘮𝘢𝘳𝘬𝘦𝘵 𝘧𝘢𝘪𝘭𝘶𝘳𝘦 kung saan pinapatay nito ang kumpetisyon sa halalan at ninanakawan ang mga ordinaryong mamamayan ng pagkakataong magsilbi sa bayan. Ayon din sa Vera Files, ang mga lalawigang kontrolado ng 𝘧𝘢𝘵 𝘥𝘺𝘯𝘢𝘴𝘵𝘪𝘦𝘴 o mga pamilyang sabay-sabay na nakaupo sa pwesto ay ang mga lugar kung saan mas talamak ang kahirapan, mas atrasado ang serbisyo, at mas marupok ang proyekto dahil sa kawalan ng pananagutan at pagsusuri.

Sa pagsisiyasat na ito, baybayin natin ang estado ng ating demokratikong sistema sa pamamagitan ng mga sumusunod na datos sa bawat munisipalidad ng Tarlac.

****

Sa huli, ang tunay na katatagan ng mga Tarlakenyo ay hindi nasusukat sa taas ng pader ng mga nasa posisyon. 𝗕𝘂𝘄𝗮𝗴𝗶𝗻 𝗮𝗻𝗴 𝗺𝗼𝗻𝗼𝗽𝗼𝗹𝘆𝗼 𝘀𝗮 𝗸𝗮𝗽𝗮𝗻𝗴𝘆𝗮𝗿𝗶𝗵𝗮𝗻—𝘂𝗽𝗮𝗻𝗴 𝗮𝗻𝗴 𝗺𝗶𝘀𝗺𝗼𝗻𝗴 𝗺𝗴𝗮 𝗺𝗮𝗺𝗮𝗺𝗮𝘆𝗮𝗻 𝗻𝗮𝗺𝗮𝗻, 𝗮𝘁 𝗵𝗶𝗻𝗱𝗶 𝗶𝗶𝘀𝗮𝗻𝗴 𝗮𝗽𝗲𝗹𝘆𝗶𝗱𝗼 𝗹𝗮𝗺𝗮𝗻𝗴 𝗮𝗻𝗴 𝗺𝗮𝗸𝗮𝘁𝗮𝘄𝗶𝗱 𝘀𝗮 𝘁𝘂𝗹𝗮𝘆 𝘁𝘂𝗻𝗴𝗼 𝘀𝗮 𝘁𝘂𝗻𝗮𝘆 𝗮𝘁 𝗽𝗮𝗻𝘁𝗮𝘆 𝗻𝗮 𝗽𝗮𝗴-𝘂𝗻𝗹𝗮𝗱.
